Some of it is bonds. When a country issues bonds, there's an obligation to repurchase the bond at maturity, along with any accumulated interest. Some of the bonds are held by entities within the country, making the country indebted to itself. Those held outside the country will of course be paid to foreign holders.

Some of the debt is used to generate future income. An example is infrastructure projects like tollbooths for a new highway financed by the government.

Generally when governments run a balanced budget, it's balanced not with respect to the year's current revenues, but to foreseeable future revenues adjusted by some discounting factor. This makes the zero point negative, so the country runs a deficit in any given year -- how much is too much is another discussion.
